data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'kahl', meaning 'to be pure, clean, or free from impurities'. In Islamic tradition, Kahlaa represents the spiritual purification of the soul, achieved through acts of obedience to Allah. The name Kahlaa carries the meaning “Pure, clean” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Kahlaa usually hope their child will grow to embody pure, clean and live with faith, good character and purpose.
